definition: Personal documents are materials originating from a person’s own life that can be used in narrative or qualitative work to help understand lived experience, identity, and life story. In this context, they are one source of information used alongside interviews, observation, and photographs.

reasons: The packet only shows that ‘personal documents’ were used as one data source alongside interviews, participant observation, and photographs; it does not define the term as materials originating from a person’s own life or as a general narrative/qualitative research method construct.
The claims about helping to understand lived experience, identity, and life story go beyond what the packet explicitly states about personal documents.

The packet does not explicitly define what “personal documents” are (e.g., that they “originate from a person’s own life”); it only states that “personal documents” were among the data-generation methods used.

While the packet indicates personal documents were used in a qualitative life-story identity study (supporting their use in such work), it does not directly support the full phrasing that they “can be used in narrative or qualitative work to help understand lived experience, identity, and life story.”

The portion stating they are “one source of information used alongside interviews, observation, and photographs” is supported (personal documents were generated alongside those methods), but this alone is not enough for all substantive claims in the definition.
